pages.title: Architecture at a glance
pages.lead: One customer-operated management platform turns an AI request into a controlled action on a named host.

rows: Jitterbit Harmony
MCP, APIM, Studio and JBMQ
AI tools, protected integration APIs and queued delivery
Dedicated management host
API, worker, PostgreSQL and HTTPS proxy
Durable jobs and execution independent of the target PA
Target hosts
Existing SSH and the JBPA lifecycle commands
Manage agents without adding a web service or listening port

pages.note: Reading path: design (1-4), controls (5-7), deployment (8-10), contracts and sources (11-13). All diagrams show the proposed product.

pages.title: One job, four clear stages
pages.lead: The installation runs independently after the first tool call returns a job ID.

rows: 1. Submit
Commit the job and dispatch outbox in one transaction. Reuse an idempotency key on retry.
A stable job ID and acceptance state
2. Queue
Publish the job reference. Dispatcher asks the parent to accept execution, then acknowledges JBMQ.
Pending dispatch or ready for execution
3. Execute
Worker claims the job and canonical host; runs the fixed JBPA caller over SSH; validates the outcome.
Running, then success, failure or reconciliation
4. Retrieve
A new tool call reads the stored result. It does not consume the queue or resume the original call.
Outcome correlated to target, action and version

pages.note: If the AI cannot poll, the user can ask to check the job later. Optional notifications inform the user; automatic chat resumption needs client support.

pages.title: Component responsibilities
pages.lead: Each component owns one part of the request, delivery or execution lifecycle.

rows: MCP server
Tool names, descriptions and input/output contracts
Configured in Jitterbit; a second custom MCP server is unnecessary
APIM + Studio
Submission, outbox relay, dispatch and status facade
Short operations call the same parent URL from every management PA
JBMQ
References awaiting dispatch and delivery dead-letter handling
Acknowledgement means durable acceptance, not installation success
Parent REST API
Authentication, action/target authorization and job APIs
No arbitrary host, shell command or secret supplied by the AI
PostgreSQL
Jobs, events, outbox, idempotency and host ownership
The authoritative job/result record; not a temporary cache
Worker + JBPA
Claim, execute, retain evidence and reconcile interruptions
One mutation per canonical host, including aliases
Inventory
Named target, host identity and access references
Mapping revision is bound to the job; no silent host redirection

pages.note: Harmony selects the PA that runs a Studio operation. The parent inventory selects the target being managed. These are separate identities. [J2]

pages.title: Technology choices and reusable value
pages.lead: Use established open-source components around the existing JBPA code; keep the default deployment bounded.

rows: Python + FastAPI / Pydantic / Uvicorn
Matches the Python execution code; typed contracts and generated OpenAPI/JSON Schema.
Shared models and tests across API/worker. Authorization still needs application rules. [T1, T2]
PostgreSQL + SQLAlchemy / Alembic
Atomic job/outbox creation, uniqueness, concurrent coordination and versioned migrations.
Durable shared service with repeatable upgrades; backup and schema operations are required. [T3]
Separate Python worker + OpenSSH
Long execution must survive API restarts; targets already expose SSH.
Reuse the fixed caller and pinned host keys; remote outcome recovery remains engineering work.
Docker Engine + Compose
Customers requested portable Linux containers and a repeatable single-host package.
Same images/topology per customer. Compose does not provide host-level HA. [T4]
NGINX Open Source
A standard TLS front door independent of application code.
Keeps API/DB ports private; a qualified customer gateway can replace it.

pages.note: SQLite fits a small local tool, but PostgreSQL is the product baseline. Kubernetes, Redis and Celery add no demonstrated requirement to this initial deployment. Licensing details are on page 12.

pages.title: Durability, state and delivery
pages.lead: Persist the business job first; use JBMQ to deliver its identity to execution.

rows: Acceptance
Create job + outbox atomically before returning. A relay repairs interrupted publication.
No accepted job depends on one successful queue-send response
Duplicate requests
Bind idempotency key to caller and canonical request. Same key/different parameters is a conflict.
Repeated delivery retrieves the same job instead of repeating a mutation
Execution states
Accepted pending dispatch -> READY -> RUNNING -> SUCCEEDED / FAILED. Unknown outcomes enter NEEDS_RECONCILIATION.
Queue publication cannot regress a running or completed job
Host ownership
Lock by canonical host, not alias. Use short DB claims and worker heartbeats.
No competing mutation; lease expiry alone never permits replay
Evidence
Record job/attempt, inventory revision, versions/digest, worker release, timestamps and safe outcome.
Results remain explainable and retrievable after restart
Queue policy
ACK after parent acceptance. Bound delivery retries and quarantine invalid references.
Installation failure is a stored result, not a delivery dead-letter event

pages.note: Submission requires the parent API/DB to be available. JBMQ buffers later dispatch outages. Its documented acknowledgement timeout is 30 minutes and maximum TTL is 10 days; jobs/outbox remain authoritative. [J1]

pages.title: Security, access and host isolation
pages.lead: A named target and fixed action cross controlled trust boundaries; credentials stay outside the AI request.

rows: AI -> MCP -> APIM
Supported client authentication and protected API/tool configuration
Jitterbit endpoints; tenant compatibility must be validated
Management PA -> parent
Private HTTPS; scoped machine identity; issuer/audience/expiry/signature validation
Proposed HTTPS :443 on dedicated management host
API / database
Non-root app process, restricted DB role and internal network
Proposed :8080 and :5432 are not host-published
Worker -> target
Pinned SSH fingerprint, fixed entry point and qualified non-interactive privilege
Worker-only SSH identity; existing target SSH port
Secrets / logs / evidence
Protected secret references, rotation, redacted output and restricted raw evidence
Separate from images, queue bodies, job results and prompts
Human identity
Verify delegated claims; never trust model-generated identity/approval headers
Shared integration account grants only its configured permissions

pages.note: No privileged containers or Docker socket mounts. Compose secret mounts are protected files, not encryption or a vault. Customers provide DNS/TLS, secret recovery and network routes.

pages.title: Failure handling and safe recovery
pages.lead: Delivery may be retried. An uncertain remote mutation must be reconciled before another action starts.

rows: Queue send / confirmation lost
Replay pending outbox; retain the same job ID.
A duplicate reference must not create another execution
Dispatch accepted / response lost
Redeliver; return existing accepted state; ACK.
Acceptance may have committed before transport failed
SSH disconnect / worker crash
Retain host ownership; inspect original attempt and remote evidence.
The target may still be installing or may already have changed
Result persistence fails
Preserve protected local/remote evidence and reconcile.
A successful remote action is not safely rerunnable merely because DB write failed
Management host / DB restored
Fence workers; restore compatible state; reconcile active jobs and stale references.
Recovered state can be older than actual target execution
Known lifecycle failure
Store failure and evidence; authorize any new mutation separately.
No automatic reinstall, Harmony deletion or generic rollback

pages.note: Required caller improvement: establish a stable remote attempt ID and evidence location before mutation. Exactly-once remote execution is not claimed; safety relies on ownership, host locking and reconciliation.

pages.title: Customer deployment and reuse
pages.lead: Ship one versioned package. Each customer supplies configuration rather than maintaining a source-code fork.

rows: Prepare
Host/runtime/config validation and support matrix
Dedicated Linux host, container runtime, routes and storage
Configure
Schemas, sanitized examples and access-policy contract
Deployment identity, TLS, IdP, secret references and inventory
Start
Pinned images, Compose, migration and readiness tooling
Persistent storage and protected credentials
Connect Jitterbit
Tested Studio kit, MCP/APIM mappings and queue instructions
Tenant/environment, entitlements, endpoints and security profiles
Onboard targets
Named-target validator, pinned-key and preflight checks
Provisioned supported hosts, SSH access and staged Harmony file
Verify
Non-mutating smoke workflow and documented acceptance tests
Authorized disposable target for live lifecycle qualification

pages.note: Use supported Harmony import/export interfaces. Where automation is unavailable, provide exact manual steps. Target provisioning and Harmony record deletion remain outside JBPA scope.

pages.title: Operate, upgrade and restore
pages.lead: The service is a reusable product only when upgrades and recovery are as repeatable as installation.

rows: Release
Immutable images, pinned dependencies, SBOM, notices, provenance and compatibility manifest
Customer secrets never enter released artifacts
Upgrade
Pause dispatch, safely drain, back up, migrate once, deploy, verify and reconcile before resuming
Management upgrades and PA upgrades are separately authorized
Backup / restore
Encrypted off-host DB/config/evidence backup and tested restoration
Agree and measure recovery objectives; no invented RPO/RTO guarantee
Monitoring
Outbox/queue age, DLQ, READY backlog, worker heartbeat, reconciliation count, DB/storage and backup age
Detect the blocked stage rather than treating all failures as installation errors
Capacity / availability
Bound worker concurrency and benchmark supported fleet load
Single-host baseline is recoverable. HA requires redundant hosts, HA DB and proven fencing
Support
Version matrix, credential rotation, diagnostics and clear operational ownership
Product code, customer infrastructure and Harmony administration have different owners

pages.note: Offer a qualified external PostgreSQL and existing-gateway configuration. Do not promise arbitrary Linux support, generic DB downgrade or safe cancellation of an executing mutation. [T4, T5]

pages.title: Production acceptance
pages.lead: The production label follows end-to-end and recovery evidence, not the choice of database or container runtime.

rows: Deployment
Fresh supported Linux host; released package; no source edits; verified configuration and migrations
Access / isolation
Denied target/action cases; token/key rotation; host-key mismatch; secret/output and network checks
Delivery / execution
Duplicate publish/dispatch, ACK loss, same-host aliases, worker/SSH/DB interruption and reconciliation
Lifecycle
Exact supported OS/PA tuples; installation, registration, health and approved old/new upgrade edges
Recovery / operation
Backup/restore drill, schema compatibility, bounded concurrency and measured operational objectives
Jitterbit / AI
Real MCP discovery, APIM response mapping, queue dispatch/ACK and later result retrieval

panels: Scoped live core lifecycle evidence exists for PA 12.10.1.1 on Ubuntu 24.04.5 amd64.
RC9 remote caller, package-changing upgrades, production sizing/artifact promotion and the proposed management stack. [R2-R4]
pages.note: Build order: contracts/persistence -> worker/recovery -> customer deployment -> Jitterbit kit -> live qualification. Close identity integration, retry entitlement, support versions and own-code licensing before release.

pages.title: Appendix A - tool and API contract
pages.lead: Business tools share a versioned parent API; delivery-control endpoints are not AI-visible tools.

rows: Install / upgrade
Named target, exact qualified version, idempotency key
POST /v1/jobs
Uninstall / diagnostics
Named target, action and idempotency key
Same async job contract; local removal only
Get job / list targets
Job ID, or caller identity
GET /v1/jobs/{id}; GET /v1/targets
Relay / dispatch
Stored outbox/job identity
GET /v1/dispatch-outbox; POST publication confirmation; POST job dispatch
Health checks
Infrastructure context
/health/live and /health/ready are separate from target health

code:
GET /v1/jobs/<UUID>
200: {"state":"SUCCEEDED","target":"qa-pa-03",
      "resolvedVersion":"12.10.1.1","result":{"status":"SUCCESS"}}

400/422 invalid; 401/403 access; 404 unknown; 409 conflict; 503 unavailable
pages.note: Examples are proposed contracts, not observed output. Diagnostic status does not prove identity-aware Harmony health. Only validated action-specific evidence establishes success.
